record.paper_title: Some open problems on excluding a uniform matroid
record.original_question: For every finite field F, are there only finitely many excluded minors, up to isomorphism, for the class of F-representable matroids?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.3 (Rota’s Conjecture, 1971). For any finite field F, there are, up to isomorphism, only finitely many excluded minors for the class of F-representable matroids.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A matroid M is said to be representable over a field F (or F-representable) if there exists a matrix with entries in F whose columns, with the linear-dependence structure inherited from the F-vector space, realize the matroid M. A matroid N is called an excluded minor (or forbidden minor) for the class of F-representable matroids if N itself is not F-representable, but every proper minor of N (i.e., every matroid obtained from N by a sequence of deletions and contractions of elements, excluding N itself) is F-representable.

Question: Is it true that for every finite field F, there are, up to isomorphism, only finitely many excluded minors for the class of F-representable matroids?
artifact.status_search_result: This is Rota's conjecture (1970). A proof was announced in 2014 by Jim Geelen, Bert Gerards, and Geoff Whittle, building on their long matroid minors project. An outline appeared in the Notices of the AMS (August 2014), and the result is widely regarded as solved, though the complete detailed write-up across many papers is still being finalized.
